::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Is matrix $A^i A^j = A^j A^i$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1648557/is-matrix-ai-aj-aj-ai), asked by [lll](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/307657/lll) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-02-10; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I want to know if $$A^i  A^j = A^j  A^i$$ holds or not. 
> It seems like an obvious, but I am wondering if there is a more formal proof
:::

Yes, it is pretty trivial, but it follows from the definition of $A^n$ as the product of a string of $n$ copies of $A$.

On one hand, $A^iA^j$ is a string of $i$ copies of $A$, followed by a string of $j$ copies of $A$.  The result is $i+j$ copies of $A$.  That is,
$$A^i A^j = A^{i+j}$$
On the other hand, $A^jA^i$ is the product of a string of $j$ copies of $A$, followed by a string of $i$ copies of $A$.  The result is $j+i$ copies of $A$.  That is,
$$A^j A^i = A^{j+i}$$
Since $i+j = j+i$, we know $A^i A^j = A^j A^i$.
